name: BRIDGE
aliases: Bridging Anticoagulation in Patients who Require Temporary Interruption of Warfarin Therapy for an Elective Invasive Procedure or Surgery
question: Does omitting perioperative low-molecular-weight heparin bridging preserve thromboembolic protection and reduce bleeding during warfarin interruption for atrial fibrillation?

design.population: Adults with atrial fibrillation or flutter receiving warfarin who required interruption for an elective operation or invasive procedure and had at least one CHADS2 stroke-risk factor.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled noninferiority randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods—Study Design, Patients and Procedures; Results—Patients, Figure 2

verdictNote: No bridging met thromboembolic noninferiority and reduced major bleeding.
takeaway: During warfarin interruption for atrial fibrillation, placebo without bridging was noninferior to dalteparin bridging for 30-day arterial thromboembolism and caused less major bleeding in BRIDGE.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Douketis JD, Spyropoulos AC, Kaatz S, et al. "Perioperative Bridging Anticoagulation in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation." *N Engl J Med.* 2015;373(9):823-833. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1501035
reports.followUp: 30 days after the procedure; final contact at 30–37 days

results.measure: 30-day stroke, transient ischemic attack or systemic embolism; risk difference in percentage points (no bridging minus bridging)
results.note: Prespecified noninferiority margin: 1.0 percentage point; upper 95% CI boundary was 0.8 percentage point.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical Analysis; Results—Study Outcomes; Table 3

results.measure: 30-day major bleeding; relative risk for no bridging versus bridging
results.note: No fatal major bleeding events occurred.

harms.label: Minor bleeding
harms.note: P<0.001 for superiority; myocardial infarction, deep-vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism and death did not differ significantly between groups.

delivery.label: Eligibility and baseline risk
delivery.value: At 108 US and Canadian sites, adults had at least 3 months of warfarin with target INR 2.0–3.0 and at least one CHADS2 stroke-risk factor; mean CHADS2 was 2.3 and few participants had scores of 5 or 6. Exclusions included mechanical heart valve, stroke or transient ischemic attack within 12 weeks, major bleeding within 6 weeks, creatinine clearance <30 mL/min, and planned cardiac, intracranial or intraspinal surgery.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods—Patients; Results—Patients, Table 1; Discussion—limitations

delivery.label: Anticoagulation schedule
delivery.value: Warfarin stopped 5 days before and restarted the evening of or day after the procedure; dalteparin 100 IU/kg subcutaneously twice daily or matching placebo started 3 days before, last preprocedure dose about 24 hours before, then resumed 12–24 hours after low-bleeding-risk or 48–72 hours after high-bleeding-risk procedures until INR was at least 2.

delivery.label: Outcome-data availability
delivery.value: 1,813/1,884 randomized patients supplied outcome data; 71 discontinued participation without outcome data.

delivery.label: Procedures performed
delivery.value: 1,722/1,884 randomized patients underwent the anticipated procedure: gastrointestinal 44.0%, cardiothoracic 17.2%, orthopedic 9.2%; 89.4% of procedures were classified as minor by the prespecified scheme.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results—Patients; Figure 2; Table S2 cited in article

delivery.label: Study drug adherence
delivery.value: All protocol-specified study drug doses were received by 86.5% before and 96.5% after the procedure.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results—Perioperative Anticoagulant Management; Table 2
